label: rem:stable-nucleus-valley
title: The stability condition restricts the hadron to the valley of stability
html:
Remark. The stability condition restricts the hadron to the valley of stability

Restricting the hadron definition. The abstract hadron (hadron) permits arbitrary multi-component composites. The stability condition restricts the physically realised nuclei to the valley of stability. Only configurations (Z, N) satisfying the beta-stability equation of the stable nucleus (beta-stability) are long-lived. Nuclei outside this valley undergo beta decay (\mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e or \mathfrak{p} \to \mathfrak{n} + e^+ + \nu_e) until they reach the stable configuration.

This is not an additional axiom. It is a strict consequence of the Skein binding Lagrangian. The parameter q determines both the strong binding (via (q + q^{-1})/2) and the Coulomb repulsion (via (q - q^{-1})/2). Their balance selects the unique stable (Z, N) for each mass number A.
